details:
An accessibility / usability annoyance with screen reader software at https://wiki.vrchat.com/ during a maintenance. There is no `<h1>` element, no `<main>` and no `<header>` or `<footer>` elements to navigate jump into. Please add these.

Steps to reproduce: Visit https://wiki.vrchat.com/ during a maintenance, try to read the page out loud in JAWS, NVDA, TalkBack or other screen reader software. Notice reading it out doesn't work well, then notice you also can't navigate the page well with accessibility software to skip the offending content / noise on the page to the main content.

Expected result: Navigate with a jump to the main content, namely a heading "Under maintenance" with the "We will be back soon! We are currently under maintenance." followed.

Actual result: The first thing read out loud is the page title "VRChat" (`<title>VRChat</title>`, indicating no error), followed by reading aloud ["underscore underscore forward slash forward slash backwards slash V forward slash" noise from the incorrectly marked up ASCII logo](https://feedback.vrchat.com/website/p/the-ascii-logo-in-vrchat-maintenance-notice-as-seen-on-vrchat-wiki-is-not-access), before getting to the actual content which says the page is unavailable. It's not possible to jump directly to the content that says the page is "unavailable".

Additional info: https://status.vrchat.com/incidents/xg3n4y6875w6
title: Add semantic HTML page structure to the maintenance notice (as seen on VRChat Wiki)
